newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- Prices flat, still recovering.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- Prices flat, still recovering.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds in early trade Wednesday were flat, and the tone remained edgy and cautious due to the market's big drop, most of which occurred Friday. That kept the lid on activity in outstanding bonds.
"At the very least (participants) want to see how the market shakes itself out after Friday's disaster," a trader said.
He speculated prices might firm slightly, provided the Treasury's sale of $12 billion of 10-year bonds goes smoothly. Tuesday's sale of three-year notes went largely as expected.
"My guess is (municipal) futures will be a little bit better unless the auction comes out today and is lousy. There might be bottom-fishing," the trader said.

While there was considerable selling interest for the two-week period leading up to last Friday, the market's retreat since then has sharply curtailed such activity. The main yardstick of the secondary market, the Standard and Poor's Blue List totaled $1.475 billion, up slightly.

The focus stayed firmly on new issues, as it has been for most of the week. New Jersey traders, who recently have seen few sales, were looking forward to the sale of $40 million of general obligations by Monmouth County.
And a New Jersey Health Agency next week plans to sell $191 million of new money and refunding bonds, according to book-runner, Goldman, Sachs & Co.
Negotiated offerings for Wednesday were expected to total $738 million in 17 sales, with a $215 million South Carolina Public Facilities offering through Merrill Lynch & Co. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 15 sales totaling $211 million were scheduled. A $39 million Cache County, Utah, offering at 1130 EDT was the largest.

New issues drew mixed results on Tuesday, as the New York City Water Finance Authority through PaineWebber sold $289 million of revenue bonds, which were repriced, with the top yield in 2021 rising to 5.50 percent from 5.474 percent.

The Authority had hoped to sell as much as $365 million of debt, but reduced the offering due to the market's volatility. it was forced to reprice the bonds both for retail investors during a presale period, and for institutional buyers.

JP Morgan Securities won $240 million Georgia bonds at a net interest cost of 4.7584 percent. The sale went off at 1100 EDT and JP Morgan reported the account closed by 1220 EDT. The noncallable deal was rated triple-A by Moody's Investors Service, Standard & Poor's Corp and Fitch Investors Service.

In Chicago futures markets, September municipal futures shed three ticks to 120-10/32. September Treasury futures slipped two ticks to 114-17/32. This left the MOB spread between the futures contracts down one tick from late Tuesday.

In secondary activity, Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority, Massachusetts, bonds of 2024, which pay a five percent coupon, were bid at 5.45 percent, NET, unchanged. And Municipal Electricity Authority, Georgia, bonds of 2026, which carry a five percent coupon, were offered at 5.35 percent, NET, unchanged.
